children.text: pratītyajānāṃ bhāvānāṃ naiḥsvābhāvyaṃ jagāda yaḥ
children.translated_text: I bow to him who declared the lack of intrinsic nature of dependently arisen entities,

children.text: taṃ namāmy asamajñānam acintyam anidarśanam ||
children.translated_text: the inconceivable and unexampled one, free from unequaled conceptual knowledge.

children.text: yathā tvayā mahāyāne dharmanairātmyam ātmanā
children.translated_text: Just as, in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, the selflessness of dharmas was known by you yourself,

children.text: viditaṃ deśitaṃ tadvad dhīmadbhyaḥ karuṇāvaśāt ||
children.translated_text: so, out of compassion, it was taught to the wise.

children.text: pratyayebhyaḥ samutpannam anutpannaṃ tvayoditam
children.translated_text: What has arisen from conditions was declared by you to be unarisen;

children.text: svabhāvena na taj jātam iti śūnyaṃ prakāśitam ||
children.translated_text: since it is not born by its own nature, it was revealed as empty.

children.text: yadvacchabdaṃ pratītyeha pratiśabdasamudbhavaḥ
children.translated_text: Just as here the arising of an echo depends upon a sound,

children.text: māyāmarīcivac cāpi tathā bhavasamudbhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and likewise as with illusion and mirage, so is the arising of existence.

children.text: māyāmarīcigandharvanagarapratibimbakāḥ
children.translated_text: Illusions, mirages, cities of the <s>Gandharvas</s>, and reflections,

children.text: yady ajātāḥ saha svapnair na syāt taddarśanādikam ||
children.translated_text: if they were not unborn, together with dreams, their being seen and so on would not occur.

children.text: hetupratyayasambhūtā yathaite kṛtakāḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Just as these, produced from causes and conditions, are regarded as fabricated,

children.text: tadvat pratyayajaṃ viśvaṃ tvayoktaṃ nātha sāṃvṛtam ||
children.translated_text: so, O Lord, the whole world born from conditions was called conventional by you.

children.text: asty etat kṛtakaṃ sarvaṃ yat kiṃcid bālalāpanam
children.translated_text: All this that is fabricated is whatever childish prattle there may be;

children.text: riktamuṣṭipratīkāśam ayathārthaprakāśitam ||
children.translated_text: it appears like an empty fist and has been shown as not corresponding to reality.

children.text: kṛtakaṃ vastu no jātaṃ tadā kiṃ vārtamānikam
children.translated_text: A fabricated thing is not born; then what could be present?

children.text: kasya nāśād atītaṃ syād utpitsuḥ kim apekṣate ||
children.translated_text: Through the destruction of what could it be past, and what does something about to arise depend upon?

children.text: svasmān na jāyate bhāvaḥ parasmān nobhayād api
children.translated_text: An entity is not born from itself, nor from another, nor from both;

children.text: na san nāsan na sadasan kutaḥ kasyodayas tadā ||
children.translated_text: not existent, not nonexistent, and not both existent and nonexistent: whence, then, could anything arise from anything?

children.text: ajāte na svabhāvo 'sti kutaḥ svasmāt samudbhavaḥ
children.translated_text: In what is unborn there is no intrinsic nature; how could there be origination from itself?

children.text: svabhāvābhāvasiddhyaiva parasmād apy asaṃbhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And precisely because the absence of intrinsic nature is established, origination from another is also impossible.

children.text: svatve sati paratvaṃ syāt paratve svatvam iṣyate
children.translated_text: If selfhood exists, otherness would exist; if otherness exists, selfhood is admitted.

children.text: āpekṣikī tayoḥ siddhiḥ pārāvāram ivoditā ||
children.translated_text: The establishment of the two is relative, as has been stated of the near and the far shore.

children.text: yadā nāpekṣate kiṃcit kutaḥ kiṃcit tadā bhavet
children.translated_text: When something does not depend on anything, how then could anything exist?

children.text: yadā nāpekṣate dīrghaṃ kuto hrasvādikaṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: When it does not depend on the long, how then could the short and the like exist?

children.text: astitve sati nāstitvaṃ dīrghe hrasvaṃ tathā sati
children.translated_text: When existence is present, nonexistence is present; likewise, when long exists, short exists.

children.text: nāstitve sati cāstitvaṃ yat tasmād ubhayaṃ na sat ||
children.translated_text: And when nonexistence is present, existence is present; therefore neither of the two is real.

children.text: ekatvaṃ ca tathānekam atītānāgatādi ca
children.translated_text: Likewise oneness and plurality, past, future, and so on,

children.text: saṃkleśo vyavadānaṃ ca samyaṅmithyā svataḥ kutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: defilement and purification, right and wrong: how could they exist by themselves?

children.text: svata eva hi yo nāsti bhāvaḥ sarvo 'sti kas tadā
children.translated_text: Indeed, when no entity exists by itself, how could all exist then?

children.text: para ity ucyate yo 'yaṃ na vinā svasvabhāvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: That which is called "other" is not apart from its own intrinsic nature.

children.text: na svabhāvo 'sti bhāvānāṃ parabhāvo 'sti no yadā
children.translated_text: When there is no intrinsic nature of entities, and no nature of another,

children.text: bhāvagrahagrahāveśaḥ paratantro 'sti kas tadā ||
children.translated_text: what then is dependent, possessed by the grasping that seizes entities?

children.text: ādāv eva samaṃ jātāḥ svabhāvena ca nirvṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: From the very beginning they are equally born and, by intrinsic nature, extinguished;

children.text: anutpannāś ca tattvena tasmād dharmās tvayoditāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and in truth they are unarisen: therefore dharmas were declared by you.

children.text: niḥsvabhāvās tvayā dhīman rūpādyāḥ saṃprakāśitāḥ
children.translated_text: O wise one, forms and the rest were clearly shown by you to be without intrinsic nature,

children.text: phenabudbudamāyābhramarīcikadalīsamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: like foam, bubbles, illusions, clouds, mirages, and plantain trunks.

children.text: indriyair upalabdhaṃ yat tat tattvena bhaved yadi
children.translated_text: If what is perceived by the senses were real in truth,

children.text: jātās tattvavido bālās tattvajñānena kiṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: foolish people would be knowers of reality; what need would there then be for knowledge of reality?

children.text: jaḍatvam apramāṇatvam athāvyākṛtatām api
children.translated_text: You have spoken of the dullness, the unreliability,

children.text: viparītaparijñānam indriyānāṃ tvam ūcivān ||
children.translated_text: the indeterminate character, and the inverted cognition of the senses.

children.text: ajñānenāvṛto yena yathāvan na prapadyate
children.translated_text: Because the world, covered by ignorance, does not understand things as they are,

children.text: lokas tena yathābhūtam iti matvā tvayoditam ||
children.translated_text: therefore, considering this, you taught what is according to reality.

children.text: astīti śāśvatī dṛṣṭir nāstīty ucchedadarśanam
children.translated_text: "It exists" is the eternalist view; "it does not exist" is the annihilationist view.

children.text: tenāntadvayanirmukto dharmo 'yaṃ deśitas tvayā ||
children.translated_text: Therefore this dharma was taught by you as free from the two extremes.

children.text: catuṣkoṭivinirmuktās tena dharmās tvayoditāḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore dharmas were declared by you to be free from the four alternatives;

children.text: vijñānasyāpy avijñeyā vācāṃ kimuta gocarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: they are unknowable even by consciousness, how much less are they within the range of speech.

children.text: svapnendrajālikodbhūtaṃ dvicandrodvīkṣaṇaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: Just as something produced in a dream or by a conjurer, or the sight of two moons,

children.text: bhūtaṃ tadvastu no bhūtaṃ tathā dṛṣṭaṃ jagat tvayā ||
children.translated_text: is a thing and yet is not a thing, so the world was seen by you.

children.text: utpannaś ca sthito naṣṭaḥ svapne yadvat sutas tathā
children.translated_text: Just as a son in a dream is born, remains, and perishes,

children.text: na cotpannaḥ sthito naṣṭa ukto loko 'rthatas tvayā ||
children.translated_text: so, in the ultimate sense, the world was said by you neither to be born, to remain, nor to perish.

children.text: kāraṇāt saṃbhavo dṛṣṭo yathā svapne tathetaraḥ
children.translated_text: Just as arising from a cause is seen in a dream, so too otherwise

children.text: saṃbhavaḥ sarvabhāvānāṃ vibhavo 'pi matas tathā ||
children.translated_text: the arising of all entities, and likewise their disappearance, is understood.

children.text: rāgādijaṃ yathā duḥkhaṃ saṃkleśasaṃsṛtī tathā
children.translated_text: Just as suffering is born from passion and the like, so too defilement and saṃsāric wandering;

children.text: saṃbhārapūraṇān muktiḥ svapnavad bhāṣitā tvayā ||
children.translated_text: and liberation through the completion of the accumulations was spoken of by you as dreamlike.

children.text: jātaṃ tathaiva no jātam āgataṃ gatam ity api
children.translated_text: What is born is, in just that way, not born; and so too what is said to have come and gone.

children.text: baddho muktas tathā jñānī dvayam icchen na tattvavit ||
children.translated_text: The bound, the liberated, and the knower: one who knows reality would not desire duality.

children.text: utpattir yasya naivāsti tasya kā nirvṛtir bhavet
children.translated_text: For that which has no arising at all, what extinction could there be?

children.text: māyāgajaprakāśatvād ādiśāntatvam arthataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because it appears like an illusory elephant, in meaning it is pacified from the beginning.

children.text: utpanno 'pi na cotpanno yadvan māyāgajo mataḥ
children.translated_text: Though arisen, it is not arisen, just as an illusory elephant is understood.

children.text: utpannaṃ ca tathā viśvam anutpannaṃ ca tattvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: So too the world is arisen, and yet in truth it is unarisen.

children.text: ameyair aprameyānāṃ pratyekaṃ nirvṛtiḥ kṛtā
children.translated_text: By immeasurable lords of the world the extinction of immeasurable beings has been accomplished, each one individually,

children.text: lokanāthair hi sattvānāṃ na kaścin mocitaś ca taiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and yet no one at all has been liberated by them.

children.text: te ca sattvāś ca no jātā ye nirvānti na te sphuṭam
children.translated_text: Those beings, and those who pass into nirvāṇa, are clearly not born;

children.text: na kaścin mocitaḥ kaiścid iti proktaṃ mahāmune ||
children.translated_text: no one has been liberated by anyone: so it has been proclaimed, O great sage.

children.text: māyākārakṛtaṃ yadvad vastu śūnyaṃ tathetarat
children.translated_text: Just as a thing made by a magician is empty, so is anything else;

children.text: vastuśūnyaṃ jagat sarvaṃ tvayoktaṃ kārakas tathā ||
children.translated_text: the whole world is empty of thinghood, and the maker as well, as you have said.

children.text: kārako 'pi kṛto 'nyena kṛtatvaṃ nātivartate
children.translated_text: The maker too, being made by another, does not pass beyond being made;

children.text: athavā tatkriyākartṛkārakasya prasajyate ||
children.translated_text: otherwise the maker of that act and agent would absurdly follow.

children.text: nāmamātraṃ jagat sarvam ity uccair bhāṣitaṃ tvayā
children.translated_text: The whole world is merely name: this was proclaimed aloud by you.

children.text: abhidhānāt pṛthagbhūtam abhidheyaṃ na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: No object denoted exists as something separate from its designation.

children.text: kalpanāmātram ity asmāt sarvadharmāḥ prakāśitāḥ
children.translated_text: For this reason all dharmas have been shown to be mere construction.

children.text: kalpanāpy asatī proktā yayā śūnyaṃ vikalpyate ||
children.translated_text: Even the construction by which emptiness is imagined has been said to be unreal.

children.text: bhāvābhāvadvayātītam anatītaṃ ca kutracit
children.translated_text: That which is beyond the duality of existence and nonexistence, and yet has not gone beyond anywhere,

children.text: na ca jñānaṃ na ca jñeyaṃ na cāsti na ca nāsti yat ||
children.translated_text: is neither cognition nor cognizable, and neither exists nor does not exist.

children.text: yan na caikaṃ na cānekaṃ nobhayaṃ na ca nobhayam
children.translated_text: That which is neither one nor many, neither both nor neither,

children.text: anālayam athāvyaktam acintyam anidarśanam ||
children.translated_text: without basis, and then unmanifest, inconceivable and without appearance,

children.text: yan nodeti na ca vyeti nocchedi na ca śāśvatam
children.translated_text: that which neither arises nor passes away, is neither annihilated nor eternal,

children.text: tad ākāśapratīkāśaṃ nākṣarajñānagocaram ||
children.translated_text: that is like space, not the sphere of knowledge of syllables.

children.text: yaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ śūnyatā saiva te matā
children.translated_text: What is dependent origination is itself regarded by you as <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness),

children.text: tathāvidhaś ca saddharmas tatsamaś ca tathāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and of that kind is the true <s>dharma</s>; equal to that is the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: tat tattvaṃ paramārtho 'pi tathatā dravyam iṣyate
children.translated_text: That reality is also the highest meaning; it is accepted as suchness and substance.

children.text: bhūtaṃ tad avisaṃvādi tadbodhād buddha ucyate ||
children.translated_text: It is real and non-deceptive; because of awakening to that, one is called a Buddha.

children.text: buddhānāṃ sattvadhātoś ca tenābhinnatvam arthataḥ
children.translated_text: For this reason, in meaning there is non-difference between the Buddhas and the realm of beings;

children.text: ātmanaś ca pareṣāṃ ca samatā tena te matā ||
children.translated_text: and therefore you hold that there is equality between oneself and others.

children.text: bhāvebhyaḥ śūnyatā nānyā na ca bhāvo 'sti tāṃ vinā
children.translated_text: Emptiness is not something other than things, and no thing exists apart from it;

children.text: tasmāt pratītyajā bhāvās tvayā śūnyāḥ prakāśitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore things born dependently have been declared by you to be empty.

children.text: hetupratyayasambhūtā paratantrā ca saṃvṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: The conventional is arisen from causes and conditions, and is dependent;

children.text: paratantra iti proktaḥ paramārthas tv akṛtrimaḥ ||
children.translated_text: it has been called dependent, but the ultimate is unmade.

children.text: svabhāvaḥ prakṛtis tattvaṃ dravyaṃ vastu sad ity api
children.translated_text: Own-being, nature, reality, substance, object, and existent as well:

children.text: nāsti vai kapito bhāvo paratantras tu vidyate ||
children.translated_text: the imagined entity does not exist, but the dependent exists.

children.text: astīti kalpite bhāve samāropas tvayoditaḥ
children.translated_text: When an imagined entity is said to exist, you have called that superimposition;

children.text: nāstīti kṛtakocchedād ucchedaś ca prakāśitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and when, because what is made is cut off, it is said not to exist, that has been explained as annihilation.

children.text: tattvajñānena nocchedo na ca śāśvatatā matā
children.translated_text: By knowledge of reality there is no annihilation, nor is eternality admitted;

children.text: vastuśūnyaṃ jagat sarvaṃ marīcipratimaṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: the whole world is held to be empty of substance, like a mirage.

children.text: mṛgatṛṣṇājalaṃ yadvan nocchedi na ca śāśvatam
children.translated_text: Just as the water of a mirage is neither annihilated nor eternal,

children.text: tadvat sarvaṃ jagat proktaṃ nocchedi na ca śāśvatam ||
children.translated_text: so the whole world has been taught to be neither annihilated nor eternal.

children.text: dravyam utpadyate yasya tasyocchedādikaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: For one for whom substance arises, annihilation and the like would follow;

children.text: antavān nāntavāṃś cāpi lokas tasya prasajyate ||
children.translated_text: for him it would follow that the world has an end and also has no end.

children.text: jñāne sati yathā jñeyaṃ jñeye jñānaṃ tathā sati
children.translated_text: When knowledge exists, the knowable exists accordingly; when the knowable exists, knowledge exists accordingly.

children.text: yatrobhayam anutpannam iti buddhaṃ tadāsti kim ||
children.translated_text: Where both are unarisen, what then exists as Buddha?

children.text: iti māyādidṛṣṭāntaiḥ sphuṭam uktvā bhiṣagvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, by means of examples such as illusion, the best of physicians spoke clearly

children.text: deśayāmāsa saddharmaṃ sarvadṛṣṭicikitsakam ||
children.translated_text: and taught the true <s>dharma</s>, the medicine for all views.

children.text: etat tat paramaṃ tattvaṃ niḥsvabhāvārthadeśanā
children.translated_text: This is that highest reality: the teaching of the meaning of lack of own-being.

children.text: bhāvagrahagṛhītānāṃ cikitseyam anuttarā ||
children.translated_text: For those seized by grasping at entities, this is the unsurpassed treatment.

children.text: dharmayājñika tenaiva dharmayajño niruttaraḥ
children.translated_text: O sacrificer by <s>dharma</s>, by this very means the unsurpassed sacrifice of <s>dharma</s>

children.text: abhīkṣṇam iṣṭas trailokye niṣkapāṭo nirargalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: has been repeatedly performed as desired in the three worlds, without deceit and without obstruction.

children.text: vastugrāhabhayocchedī kutīrthyamṛgabhīkaraḥ
children.translated_text: Destroying fear born from grasping at objects, terrifying the deer of false teachers,

children.text: nairātmyasiṃhanādo 'yam adbhuto naditas tvayā ||
children.translated_text: this wondrous lion's roar of selflessness has been roared by you.

children.text: śūnyatādharmagambhīrā dharmabherī parāhatā
children.translated_text: The deep <s>dharma</s>-drum of emptiness has been struck,

children.text: naiḥsvābhāvyamahānādo dharmaśaṅkhaḥ prapūritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the <s>dharma</s>-conch of the great sound of lack of own-being has been fully blown.

children.text: dharmayautukam ākhyātaṃ buddhānāṃ śāsanāmṛtam
children.translated_text: The bridal gift of <s>dharma</s>, the nectar of the Buddhas' teaching, has been proclaimed;

children.text: nītārtham iti nirdiṣṭaṃ dharmāṇāṃ śūnyataiva hi ||
children.translated_text: indeed, the emptiness of dharmas has been specified as having definitive meaning.

children.text: yā tūtpādanirodhādisattvajīvādideśanā
children.translated_text: But the teaching about arising and cessation, and about beings, souls, and the like,

children.text: neyārthā ca tvayā nātha bhāṣitā saṃvṛtiś ca sā ||
children.translated_text: was spoken by you, O Lord, as having a meaning to be interpreted; that is the conventional truth.

children.text: prajñāpāramitāmbhodher yo 'tyantam pāram āgataḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever has gone completely to the far shore of the ocean of the perfection of wisdom

children.text: sa puṇyaguṇaratnāḍhyas tvadguṇārṇavapāragaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is rich in jewels of merit and virtue, and has crossed beyond the ocean of your qualities.

children.text: iti stutvā jagannātham acintyam anidarśanam
children.translated_text: Having thus praised the Lord of the world, inconceivable and without appearance,

children.text: yad avāptaṃ mayā puṇyaṃ tenāstu tvatsamaṃ jagat ||
children.translated_text: by whatever merit I have obtained, may the world thereby become equal to you.

children.text: ity acintyastavaḥ samāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus the Acintyastava is completed.
